author: Irenaeus of Lyons
occasion: Irenaeus writes to Victor of Rome during a dispute over the day and form of the Paschal fast. The surviving fragments urge peace and show that earlier Roman bishops maintained communion with those who observed a different custom, but they do not explicitly mention excommunication.
argument: Irenaeus argues that differences over the day and manner of the Paschal fast are long-standing and do not break the unity of faith. He shows that earlier Roman bishops, though not observing the Asian custom themselves, lived in peace with those who did and even sent the Eucharist to them. He recounts the meeting of Polycarp and Anicetus in Rome, where the two men disagreed on the fast but remained in communion, with Anicetus yielding the Eucharist to Polycarp as a sign of respect. The surviving fragments close with a warning that anyone who can do good to a neighbor and fails to do so will be considered a stranger to the love of the Lord.

outline.move: Irenaeus describes the variety in the duration of the Paschal fast, insists this diversity is old and compatible with peace and unity of faith, and recounts how earlier Roman bishops and Polycarp kept communion despite differing customs.
Irenaeus warns that anyone who can do good to a neighbor and fails to do so will be considered a stranger to the love of the Lord.

_unresolved_facts.claim: they do not explicitly mention excommunication
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καὶ οὐδέ ποτε διὰ τὸ εἶδος τοῦτο ἀπεβλήθησαν τινές
_unresolved_facts.fix: the source explicitly states that no one was ever rejected (ἀπεβλήθησαν) on account of this matter
Πίον is accusative singular; the nominative form is Πίος (Pius)
Ὑγῖνόν is accusative singular; the nominative form is Ὑγῖνος (Hyginus)
Τελεσφόρον is accusative singular; the nominative form is Τελεσφόρος (Telesphorus)
Ξύστον is accusative singular; the nominative form is Ξύστος (Xystus)
Ἀνίκητον is accusative singular; the nominative form is Ἀνίκητος (Anicetus)
Πολυκάρπου (genitive) and Πολύκαρπον (accusative); the nominative form is Πολύκαρπος (Polycarp)
Ἰωάννου is genitive singular; the nominative form is Ἰωάννης (John)

_unresolved_facts.claim: with Anicetus yielding the Eucharist to Polycarp as a sign of respect
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ παρεχώρησεν ὁ Ἀνίκητος τὴν εὐχαριστίαν τῷ Πολυκάρπῳ κατ’ ἐντροπὴν δηλονότι
_unresolved_facts.fix: Anicetus yielded/gave place (παρεχώρησεν) the Eucharist to Polycarp in the church, out of deference/respect (κατ' ἐντροπὴν δηλονότι) — the Greek suggests Anicetus made room for Polycarp to celebrate rather than simply 'yielding' it
